title: From spreading to a measurable distance
spoken: The model coordinate root mean square displacement equals the square root of two times the diffusion coefficient times the observation interval.
explanation: Squaring measures spread without cancellation between directions. Taking the positive square root turns squared distance back into a distance. Four times the observation interval gives twice the model RMS, not four times.

notes.title: A model relation
notes.explanation: This equality concerns the ideal model. A finite synthetic ensemble fluctuates around it; its sample RMS is displayed separately.

notes.title: Coordinate RMS
notes.explanation: One coordinate, not the total three-dimensional distance. Model RMS and sample RMS have different meanings.

notes.title: Why a square root?
notes.explanation: Two D t has units of squared length. Its positive square root has units of length and defines the typical displacement.

notes.title: Build the mean square
notes.explanation: Independent zero-mean increments add their variances. The definition of D makes the coordinate mean square equal to 2 D t.

notes.title: Diffusion coefficient
notes.explanation: This is the accepted model diffusivity, not a rate inferred from the synthetic data.

notes.title: Observation interval
notes.explanation: This is the interval used for the displayed displacement, not the simulation frame rate. Re-observing the trial preserves its paths.

assumptions: Independent, zero-mean Gaussian displacement increments in a homogeneous liquid.
One-coordinate model statistic, not a measured speed or a sample estimate.
The overdamped regime is assumed rather than established from additional particle and fluid measurements.
